mainTopic: Spreading a cloth to interrupt a meal for קידוש and הבדלה, when one may start a meal on ערב שבת and ערב פסח, and whether קידוש heard in the בית הכנסת counts
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that says one must interrupt a meal for הבדלה just as for קידוש. The גמרא suggests that 'interrupt' means removing the table (עקירת שולחן), which would challenge the ruling that a cloth is enough. It rejects this: spreading a cloth (מפה) over the food also counts. A story about רבה בר רב הונא at the house of the ריש גלותא, along with a supporting ברייתא, shows that if the table is already out, one spreads a cloth and makes קידוש. Next, the גמרא points out two ברייתות that contradict each other. One says רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree that one may not start a meal; the other says they agree that one may. The first refers to ערב פסח. The second refers to before the ninth hour, while their argument is only about after the ninth hour. Finally, a new topic begins: people who heard קידוש in the בית הכנסת. רב rules that they fulfilled קידוש but not the ברכה on wine, and שמואל's differing view continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quoted source: interrupting for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source line: just as one interrupts a meal for קידוש, one also interrupts for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too one interrupts for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of a source the גמרא was already quoting. It sets up the next question: what exactly does 'interrupt' mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source compares הבדלה to קידוש: in both cases you must stop your meal. It is quoted as a challenge to the view that spreading a cloth is enough. The next step argues that 'interrupt' means removing the table.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing that separates שבת from the weekday at its end

phrases.english: so too one interrupts for havdala.
phrases.notes: Tail end of a ברייתא whose quotation began on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא quoted on the previous amud as an objection to the ruling that one spreads a cloth and makes קידוש.
steps.raayaObject: Not a support. The source is quoted as the basis of the challenge developed in step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source comparing interrupting for הבדלה to interrupting for קידוש

steps.title: Does 'interrupt' mean removing the table?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'interrupt' must mean physically removing the table, which would challenge the view that spreading a cloth is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'interrupt' mean? Doesn't it mean removing the table?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'interrupt' means. It suggests the word means taking the table away completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'interrupt' means עקירת שולחן (removing the table), then simply covering the food would not be enough. That would contradict the view that one may spread a cloth and make קידוש. The question is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not…? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: What is meant by 'one interrupts'?
Is it not referring to removing the table?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the source just quoted to draw a specific conclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that spreading a cloth over the food is enough to make קידוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'interrupting' means removing the table, then covering the food would not count.

steps.title: No, it means spreading a cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: 'interrupt' can simply mean spreading a cloth over the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means spreading a cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'interrupt' does not have to mean removing the table. Covering the food with a cloth is a valid way to interrupt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof falls away because the word 'interrupt' fits a smaller action just as well. Spreading a מפה separates the meal from the blessing. So the view that a cloth is enough stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth / tablecloth spread over the food

steps.whatToRemember: 'Interrupting' a meal for קידוש or הבדלה can be done by spreading a cloth over the food. You do not need to remove the table.

phrases.english: No, it refers to spreading a cloth.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that 'interrupt' means removing the table
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'interrupt' is also satisfied by spreading a cloth, so it proves nothing.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא spreads a cloth and makes קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A story: at the ריש גלותא's house, a table was brought before רבה בר רב הונא, and he spread a cloth over it and made קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא came to the house of the ריש גלותא. They brought a table before him. He spread a cloth and made קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the practice in action. Food was already on the table, so רבה בר רב הונא covered it and made קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up what step 3 said: you do not need to remove the table. Covering it is enough. It shows an actual sage doing this in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, leader of the Jews in Babylonia
A small table / tray of food

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna
happened to come to the house of the Exilarch;
they brought a table before him;
he spread a cloth and recited kiddush.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ruling of step 3 being practiced by a sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the table was already brought, one spreads a cloth and makes קידוש.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports spreading a cloth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one should not bring the table before קידוש. If it was already brought, one spreads a cloth and makes קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: they agree that one does not bring the table unless he made קידוש. If he did bring it, he spreads a cloth and makes קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as the story. Ideally, bring the table only after קידוש; if it is already there, cover it and make קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives formal source support to the practice of רבה בר רב הונא. It sets up two levels: the ideal (no table before קידוש) and what to do after the fact (cover it with a cloth).

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (supporting source)

steps.whatToRemember: Ideally the table is brought only after קידוש. If it was brought earlier, spread a cloth over it and make קידוש.

phrases.english: It was also taught so (in a baraita):
(and they agree) that one does not bring the table
unless he has made kiddush;
and if he did bring it,
he spreads a cloth and makes kiddush.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ברייתא source for the story in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Spreading a cloth is enough when the table is already present before קידוש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'if he brought it, he spreads a cloth and makes kiddush'

steps.title: Two ברייתות contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree that one may not start a meal. Another says they agree that one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: they agree that one does not begin. Another ברייתא teaches: they agree that one does begin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: two ברייתות seem to say opposite things. Both describe what רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree on about starting a meal close to evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue about eating late on ערב שבת. Yet one source says they agree you may not start a meal, and another says they agree you may. The גמרא must find two different cases to make both sources true.

phrases.english: One baraita teaches:
they agree that one does not begin (a meal);
and another baraita teaches:
they agree that one does begin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא שָׁוִין שֶׁאֵין מַתְחִילִין וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ שָׁוִין שֶׁמַּתְחִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about starting a meal on ערב שבת or ערב פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the two ברייתות about what רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree on
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources claim agreement, but on opposite rulings.
steps.confusionAlert: 'They agree' (שוין) refers to רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, who usually argue about eating late on ערב שבת. Each ברייתא is describing a case where their argument does not apply.

steps.title: The 'may not begin' ברייתא fits ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא (they agree one may not begin) is easy to explain: it refers to ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, the ברייתא that says they agree one may not begin: you can find it on ערב פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first ברייתא easily: on ערב פסח, everyone agrees you may not start a meal late in the day. This is the first half of a 'בשלמא… אלא' structure, setting up a problem with the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח even רבי יוסי admits that one should not start a meal, so that he eats the מצה with appetite. That gives the first ברייתא a clear case. The real difficulty is still the second ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this part is fine (sets up 'but the other part is hard')
You can find it (a case where it applies)

phrases.english: Granted, that which was taught:
'they agree that one does not begin' —
you can find it on the eve of Passover;

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא שָׁוִין שֶׁאֵין מַתְחִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves half of the contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the ruling to a specific day (ערב פסח)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seem to be about the same situation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'may not begin' ברייתא is about ערב פסח, where all agree.

steps.title: When could they agree that one may begin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the second ברייתא (they agree one may begin) applies. It cannot mean ערב שבת, because there they argue.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא that says they agree one may begin — when? If you say on ערב שבת — they argue about that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now presses on the second ברייתא. It cannot find a case: ערב שבת will not work, because רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי openly argue about that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'they agree one may begin' would clash with the known argument about eating on ערב שבת. So the second ברייתא seems to have no case where it fits. That is the sharp question the next step must answer.

phrases.english: But that which was taught:
'they agree that one begins' — when?
If we say on Shabbat eve —
but they do disagree (about that)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא דְּתַנְיָא שָׁוִין שֶׁמַּתְחִילִין אֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'אלא' half of the בשלמא structure: the second ברייתא remains hard.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that says רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי agree one may begin a meal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only natural case is ערב שבת, but there רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי are known to disagree.

steps.title: Before the ninth hour vs. after the ninth hour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the agreement is about starting a meal before the ninth hour of the day; their argument is about after the ninth hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: here — before nine hours; there — after nine hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem by splitting the time of day. Before the ninth hour everyone agrees you may start a meal; their argument is only about after the ninth hour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'they agree one may begin' ברייתא is about earlier in the afternoon, when there is no concern. The argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי applies only later, after the ninth hour, close to evening. So all the sources now fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces a resolution)
Nine (the ninth hour of the day)

steps.whatToRemember: All agree that a meal may be started before the ninth hour of ערב שבת. רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי argue only about after the ninth hour. On ערב פסח, all agree not to start a meal late in the day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the time framework for starting a meal before שבת and before the סדר, which shapes how much appetite one keeps for the evening meal.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here — before nine hours;
there — after nine hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן קוֹדֶם תִּשְׁעָה כָּאן לְאַחַר תִּשְׁעָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting cases by time of day (כאן… כאן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'may begin' ברייתא has no fitting case, since ערב שבת is disputed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The agreement is about before the ninth hour; the dispute is about after the ninth hour.

steps.title: רב: קידוש in Shul Counts for קידוש but Not for the Wine
steps.stepSummary: About people who heard קידוש in the בית הכנסת, רב rules that they fulfilled קידוש. They did not fulfill the ברכה on wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those people who made קידוש in the בית הכנסת: רב said, they did not fulfill their obligation for the wine, but they did fulfill their obligation of קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It describes people who heard קידוש in the בית הכנסת and brings רב's ruling about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits the case into two separate obligations. The obligation of קידוש itself (declaring the holiness of שבת) is done, so they do not need to repeat קידוש at home. But the ברכה of בורא פרי הגפן said in shul does not cover drinking wine at home, so they must make a new ברכה on wine there.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogue. In those times קידוש was said there on Friday night after davening.
The declaration of the holiness of שבת or יום טוב, usually said over a cup of wine.
They fulfilled their obligation (literally, they went out of the hands of the obligation).
The obligation connected to the wine, meaning the ברכה over the wine.
A leading early אמורא in Bavel, often found in a disagreement with שמואל.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב means they must make קידוש again at home. He says the opposite: קידוש is done. The only thing missing is the ברכה on the wine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the start of a well-known disagreement between רב and שמואל. It ties into the rule that קידוש should be made where one eats the meal (קידוש במקום סעודה), which comes up shortly in the sugya.

phrases.english: Those people
phrases.notes: The גמרא sets up the case before giving the ruling.

phrases.english: who made kiddush in the synagogue,
phrases.notes: They heard קידוש in shul, which was the custom on Friday night.

phrases.english: Rav said:
they have not fulfilled their obligation of the wine,
phrases.notes: They need a new ברכה on wine before drinking at home.

phrases.english: but they have fulfilled their obligation of kiddush.
phrases.notes: They do not need to repeat קידוש itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָם בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the laws of קידוש. It does not depend on the ערב פסח / ninth-hour discussion in Steps 6 through 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing קידוש in the בית הכנסת fulfills the obligation of קידוש. It does not cover the ברכה on wine for drinking at home.

steps.title: שמואל Begins His Opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces שמואל, who will give a different ruling about people who heard קידוש in shul. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring שמואל's opinion on the same case, and his actual words come in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גמרא brings a second opinion on the same case right after רב, it usually signals a disagreement. Expect שמואל to rule differently about whether these people fulfilled קידוש.

keyTerms.meaning: A great אמורא in Bavel and the frequent partner in debate of רב.
And שמואל said. This formula introduces a second opinion on the same issue.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: His ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second, likely opposing, opinion on the case רב just ruled on in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. שמואל's ruling appears on the next amud.
